- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Nataraja: Shiva as the cosmic dancer symbolizing the rhythm and harmony of the universe.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ardhanarishvara: Shiva as half male and half female, representing the union of opposites.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Mahakala: Shiva as the lord of time and death, symbolizing the cyclical nature of life.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Bhairava: Shiva in his fierce form, representing his role as the destroyer of evil.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Lingam: Shiva in the form of a cylindrical or oval-shaped stone symbolizing his creative energy.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Dakshinamurthy: Shiva as the teacher of knowledge and wisdom.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Pashupati: Shiva as the lord of animals, representing his concern for all living beings.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Each form represents a different aspect of Shiva's nature and highlights a different aspect of his divinity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The various forms of Shiva are important in Hindu mythology and worship as they remind devotees of Shiva's multi-faceted nature and provide a path to connect with him in different ways.
